Chapter 3: Focusing on Strengths—Leveraging Core Competencies
So, once you’ve got your priorities straight, the next big question is—how do you actually tackle them? A lot of us, without even realizing it, try to do everything ourselves. We spread our energy thin, juggling all sorts of tasks, and end up feeling stretched and drained. But here’s the thing—not every activity is created equal. Some things play right to our strengths and give us that “in the zone” feeling, while others just leave us tired and unsatisfied.
That’s where the idea of core competencies comes in. Think of core competencies as the skills or activities that just click for you—things that feel natural, produce great results, and leave you feeling energized. At work, maybe it’s leading a team, solving tough problems, or building strong connections. At home, it could be anything from nurturing your kids, to organizing the household, or just creating a warm, welcoming atmosphere.
But how do you figure out what your true strengths are? It starts with a little honest reflection. Ask yourself: What kinds of tasks really give you a sense of accomplishment? Where do people come to you for advice or help? And maybe most importantly, what leaves you feeling energized instead of worn out?
Once you spot your core strengths, the next step is pretty simple—spend more time on them. That usually means letting go of some things that don’t play to your strengths. Now, don’t get me wrong—it’s not about avoiding hard or boring work altogether. It’s about making sure your time goes where it matters most.
This is where outsourcing or minimizing really pays off. All those routine or low-value tasks? Many of them can be delegated, automated, or just simplified. Picture this: if you’re someone who’s great at big-picture strategy, but paperwork slows you down, maybe it’s time to bring in a virtual assistant or use some scheduling apps. Or, if you love story time with your kids but dread meal planning, you might swap chores with your partner or even try a meal kit service.
So, how do you put this into action? Start by making a list of everything you do in a typical week. Mark which tasks truly play to your strengths—and which don’t. For those that aren’t your core strengths, see if there’s a way to delegate, outsource, or just do them less often. Then, take the time you’ve saved and double down on the activities that matter most to you.
Remember, this isn’t about dodging responsibility. It’s about giving yourself the chance to make your biggest impact—and actually enjoy the process. When you focus your efforts on what you do best, you’ll notice your productivity go up, but you’ll also feel more fulfilled. Your week starts to look less like a never-ending to-do list, and more like a chance to thrive right where you shine.
